main_topics.reason: The user came in because nausea after the weekly dose had become severe and described feeling unwell through Saturday and Sunday.
The user wondered whether to quit, then sought options for controlling nausea while keeping a medicine that helps their joints.
The user asked whether taking folic acid on the same day as methotrexate was a problem and agreed to change the timing.
The user asked whether injectable methotrexate could make a difference and said they were scared of injecting themselves.
The user asked whether an anti-nausea medicine was safe to take with methotrexate.
The user asked what to say at the upcoming appointment and said they would write down the suggested questions.
The user said methotrexate had made their hands much better, which informed their wish not to stop if avoidable.

output.summary: The user considered stopping methotrexate because of severe nausea after the weekly dose, despite improved joints. They explored folic acid timing, dose-splitting, anti-nausea medicine and injections, and prepared questions for a doctor visit in about two weeks. The user felt much better and said they would continue for now and try the agreed changes; no urgent symptoms were reported.
